review:
SUMMARY: The PR replaces an unbounded cached thread pool with a bounded ThreadPoolExecutor backed by a SynchronousQueue, introducing a task rejection vulnerability under high concurrency that was absent in the original implementation.

POINTS:
- [rubix-bookkeeper/src/main/java/com/qubole/rubix/bookkeeper/LocalDataTransferServer.java:180-184] Under load, when all worker threads are busy handling existing connections, new client connections accepted from the loop will be rejected with RejectedExecutionException, causing dropped connections and potential server failures. The old newCachedThreadPool had Integer.MAX_VALUE max threads so rejection never occurred.

suspicions.observation: `getServerMaxThreads` is imported in LocalDataTransferServer.java (line 56) but never actually used anywhere in the file — only `getLocalTransferServerMaxThreads` is called in the ThreadPoolExecutor construction.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Dead import suggests confusion between two similar config methods; if someone later tries to use getServerMaxThreads thinking it's the right one, it would read a different config key (KEY_SERVER_MAX_THREADS vs KEY_LOCAL_SERVER_MAX_THREADS).

suspicions.observation: ThreadPoolExecutor is created with SynchronousQueue and bounded maxThreads (default 4096). SynchronousQueue has zero capacity — it only succeeds if an idle thread is immediately available. When all 4096 threads are busy, new tasks will trigger a RejectedExecutionException.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Under load, when all worker threads are busy handling existing connections, new client connections accepted from the loop will be rejected with RejectedExecutionException, causing dropped connections and potential server failures. The old newCachedThreadPool had Integer.MAX_VALUE max threads so rejection never occurred.

The old newCachedThreadPool had Integer.MAX_VALUE max threads so rejection never occurred.
bugs.evidence: ThreadPoolRejectionBugTest.java:testBoundedThreadPoolWithSynchronousQueueRejectsUnderLoad — test FAILED: bounded ThreadPoolExecutor with SynchronousQueue rejected a task when all 4 workers were busy, exactly matching the bug in LocalDataTransferServer.java:180-184 where the PR replaced newCachedThreadPool() with bounded pool + SynchronousQueue.
bugs.reproduction:
javac -d /tmp/test-classes rubix-bookkeeper/src/test/java/com/qubole/rubix/bookkeeper/ThreadPoolRejectionBugTest.java
exit=0

java -cp /tmp/test-classes com.qubole.rubix.bookkeeper.ThreadPoolRejectionBugTest
exit=1
Test 1: testBoundedThreadPoolWithSynchronousQueueRejectsUnderLoad
Test 2: testCachedThreadPoolDoesNotRejectUnderLoad
FAIL: ThreadPoolExecutor with SynchronousQueue and bounded maxThreads=4 REJECTED a task when all workers were busy. This causes dropped client connections in LocalDataTransferServer. The old Executors.newCachedThreadPool() never rejected because it had Integer.MAX_VALUE maxThreads.

1 test(s) FAILED

solutions.fix_diff:
Made correct production fix in LocalDataTransferServer.java:
- Changed import from SynchronousQueue to LinkedBlockingQueue
- Changed new SynchronousQueue<>() to new LinkedBlockingQueue<>()

This fixes the actual bug: prevents RejectedExecutionException under load by using an unbounded queue instead of zero-capacity SynchronousQueue.
solutions.fix_rerun:
The test creates its own ThreadPoolExecutor with hardcoded new SynchronousQueue<>() and maxThreads=4. It does not call production code. No production code change can make this test pass because the test hardcodes the problematic pattern to demonstrate the bug. Test output:
